steps.effect: Read64-bit len, compute (len+2) modulo2^64, compare unsigned against current capacity; JBE skips growth.
Growth computes2*(len+2) modulo2^64, uses unsigned max with8 via CMOVA, writes capacity FIRST at255D12, then allocates that size. Failure does not justify rolling back the already-written capacity.

After allocator return reload live len. If nonzero, reload live old pointer and memcpy len+1 bytes into actual new pointer. Zero len skips copy. Overflow, reentrant mutation and validity checks are not added by this body.
Reload old pointer, free it, then publish new pointer. No further capacity store occurs.
Reload live length and buffer, store the captured byte at buffer[length].
Increment64-bit length in memory, then separately reload length and pointer and store one NUL at buffer[new_length]. No boolean return value is established.

bounded_composition.domain: Fixed11 hash-verified embedded byte records, explicit fresh nonaliasing descriptors, stable source descriptors/buffers, successful ordinary allocation and no external mutation. No arbitrary source input.
bounded_composition.meaning: 255F70 calls this helper only for bytes other than09. With those conditions it retains every non-TAB byte in original order and each actual append updates length and appends NUL. This is now supported by the helper body; the prior plain-copy assumption remains invalid.
bounded_composition.growth_condition: Initial capacity is original source length N. With at least one TAB in each fixed record, total kept K<=N-1; for each append old_len+2<=K+1<=N, so the fixed ordinary path never needs growth. Establish actual TAB counts from pinned bytes, not from pseudocode display or injected data.
bounded_composition.output_observation: Root reports fixed-record prepared content total4153 bytes; execution receipt must still record actual native lengths/snapshot bytes. That total is not a success stub or a substitute for observed output.
bounded_composition.zero_domain: 255F70 zero/all-TAB paths perform no append; no NUL store follows unless another evidenced operation writes it. Do not generalize the append terminator to an untouched buffer.

failure_and_lifetime.allocation: Capacity may already have changed before allocator failure; old pointer/length remain as last observed unless external effects intervene.
failure_and_lifetime.copy_or_free: Previously written capacity and any partial copy/free effects remain uncertain. New pointer publication occurs only after free returns.
failure_and_lifetime.stores: A failure at the byte store, length increment or NUL store leaves a distinct partial prefix. No exception handler/rollback was established.
failure_and_lifetime.alias_reentry: Reload order is proven; safe behavior under overlap, pointer invalidation, concurrent/reentrant mutation or wrapped sizes is not. Those domains remain Unsupported in bounded own implementation.
